speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate the cause of your systemic hypertension. To begin, how old are you, and have you noticed any headaches, blurred vision, or swelling in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you are a 5-year-old boy with no medication history or family heart disease, your hypertension is likely secondary to a kidney or adrenal issue. Has anyone ever measured your blood pressure at home, or have you experienced any new symptoms like excessive thirst, weight loss, or abdominal pain since your last visit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The finding of hypertension isolated to the right upper extremity is classic for coarctation of the aorta, where the narrowing obstructs blood flow to the lower body. I need to confirm this with imaging before finalizing the plan.

REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram.
